alt: Poster: Equity derivatives expiry under SEBI's framework - expiries limited to Tuesday or Thursday, one weekly benchmark index options contract per exchange, other contracts minimum one-month tenor expiring in the last week of the month
text:
An exchange can no longer expire its equity derivatives on any weekday it likes: SEBI limits it to Tuesday or Thursday.

Under SEBI circular SEBI/HO/MRD/MRD-TPD-1/P/CIR/2025/76 dated 26 May 2025, expiries of all equity derivatives contracts of an exchange are uniformly limited to either Tuesday or Thursday. Each exchange may offer one weekly benchmark index options contract, on its chosen day. Exchanges must also seek SEBI's prior approval before modifying the settlement day of their derivatives contracts.

Other contracts (benchmark index futures, non-benchmark index futures and options, single stock futures and options) must have a minimum tenor of one month and expire in the last week of the month. In practice, NSE's circular moved expiry for new contracts from Thursday to Tuesday from 1 September 2025, with monthly contracts expiring on the last Tuesday of the month.

Our reading: a fixed weekday framework makes the expiry calendar easier to plan around, but practitioners should always confirm the day and holiday adjustments from the latest exchange circular. This is an opinion, not advice.

For practitioners: has the single-weekday expiry framework changed how you plan roll-overs or client communication around expiry week?
